title: Impressions of a parade and church service
summary: Bull describes the parade he played in and a local church service that astonished him, and Allen asks about the hats worn.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, I don't know. I think they're overall much the same because I think the situation is the same. Probably I've accepted the grim fate a bit more than I did last week. All I can say is it's a pity that the last, or the seemingly last stronghold, if you like to call it that of proper music, has to be in those sort of hands. It's a bit of a pity. Anyway, my impressions of the place, as you said last week, have changed because I did that parade on Sunday and heard a church service and all this sort of business. And it does, as you say, it completely changes the outlook on the thing. It was, I really enjoyed it. You weren't there, were you? No, I haven't. This is one up at Harnville. And it was very pleasing to me because it was just like what I hoped it would be like. And they had a Marlis parade with all the fellas in their black suits and black Homburg hats and all the lodge belts and collars and big banners and all that sort of stuff. And all the women were dressed in white and had a big second line and everything. And of course, I was lucky enough to play with the band. And then the church service was something that knocked me right out. Just a local, ordinary church service and a little old wooden church and just sort of, you know, a local housewife's choir. And it was tremendous, phenomenal. That knocked me right out, that church service. The singing was incredible. As I said on the day, if they enjoyed themselves in church like that in Australia, more people would go.
Did they have bowlers on? Any of the men? Derbies? Or was it all Homburg?
I don't know. There might have. I think there were a few. But they were mainly those big black, turned up side Homburgs, you know, that sort of thing.
